column11: derived from CROWN, the Phase 3 that registered first-line lorlatinib: at the five-year landmark, progression-free survival was 60% with lorlatinib against 8% with crizotinib, and the median was not reached (Solomon BJ et al., Lorlatinib versus crizotinib in patients with advanced ALK-positive non-small cell lung cancer: 5-year outcomes from the Phase III CROWN study, Journal of Clinical Oncology 2024;42:3400-3409). A constant hazard that leaves 60% alive and progression-free at five years is -ln(0.60)/5 = 0.10217 a year, so 1 - exp(-0.10217) = 0.0971 of the stock stops each year

there is no lorlatinib ovarian cancer programme. The sole study behind this unit, NCT05059522, is 'Continued Access Study for Participants Deriving Benefit in Pfizer-Sponsored Avelumab Parent Studies That Are Closing': a rollover protocol registered 2021-09-28, Phase 3, Active not recruiting, primary completion 2026-12-31, listing eight interventions (avelumab, lorlatinib, talazoparib, pemetrexed, axitinib, CMP-001, utomilumab, PF-04518600) across five conditions. The ovarian cancer arm belongs to the avelumab parent studies. Pfizer's Q1 2026 Pipeline Update (5 May 2026) carries no lorlatinib programme at all outside its approved ALK-positive NSCLC use
